issues.title: Logger uses direct logging.getLogger initialization
issues.description: The rule requires logger instances to be created using the pattern `logger: "logging.Logger" = get_logger("module_name")` from prefect.logging, but the code uses the direct `logging.getLogger(__name__)` pattern instead.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Logger for SDK fetcher operations
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
issues.rule_name: Logger Instances Must Follow Standard Initialization Pattern

issues.title: Incorrect deployment filtering breaks full-name matching
issues.description: The deployment filtering logic checks `dep.name not in deployment_names` instead of checking `full_name not in deployment_names`. This causes the filter to incorrectly evaluate when users specify deployment names in 'flow-name/deployment-name' format. When a user provides a full deployment name like 'my-flow/production', the code checks if 'production' (the short name) is in the list containing 'my-flow/production', which fails, causing the deployment to enter the fallback matching logic unnecessarily. This breaks the fast-path check and could lead to incorrect filtering behavior where deployments are included or excluded inappropriately.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# If filtering by deployment name, check the full name matches
        full_name = f"{flow_name}/{dep.name}"
        if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:
            # Only include if the full name matches (filter was by name parts)
            # Skip if user specified full names and this doesn't match
            found_match = False

issues.title: Missing type validation for work pool job variables schema
issues.description: The code removes the `isinstance(variables, dict)` type check before assigning `base_job_template["variables"]` to `job_vars_schema`. The `job_vars_schema` variable is typed as `dict[str, Any]` and is expected to be a dictionary throughout the SDK generation process. If `base_job_template["variables"]` contains a non-dict value (like a list, string, or other type due to malformed work pool configuration), this will cause type inconsistencies that could lead to runtime errors in downstream code that expects a dict, such as the template renderer or SDK generator that processes the schema.

issues.title: Removed strict zip validation enables silent data corruption
issues.description: The code removes `strict=True` from the `zip(pool_names_list, results)` call in the work pool parallel fetching logic. The strict parameter ensures that both iterables have the same length and raises a ValueError if they don't match. Without it, if there's a mismatch between the number of work pool names and the results from `asyncio.gather()` (which should never happen in correct code but could occur due to bugs in the async gather logic or unexpected exceptions), the zip will silently truncate to the shorter sequence. This means some work pool results could be dropped or mismatched with the wrong names, leading to incorrect work pool metadata in the generated SDK without any warning or error.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20241 - Add documentation for prefect sdk generate CLI

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds two docs pages for the beta `prefect sdk generate` command (a how-to guide and a CLI reference), adds them to `docs/docs.json`, and makes four unrelated edits to `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`. The docs are mostly accurate: the CLI reference matches the Typer help text in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`, and the guide's `with_options`, `with_infra`, `run_async`, and `from_name` usage matches `templates/sdk.py.jinja`. However, the guide's "Combine multiple filters" example will fail at runtime, because flow and deployment filters are ANDed on the server.

The fetcher edits are not described in the PR and are not docs. One of them changes deployment-name matching: the gate now compares `dep.name` instead of `full_name`, which skips the short-name branch for short filters and silently drops the ambiguous-short-name warning. The existing test for that warning would fail. The PR also leaves a module-level `logger` between imports, which ruff reports as E402, and removes a dict type guard and `strict=True` with no stated reason.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The deployment-filter change in fetcher.py is a behavioral regression that breaks an existing test's expectations, and the guide's combined-filter example produces NoDeploymentsError. Both should be fixed before merge. The lint failure and the unexplained removal of the dict guard should also be resolved or justified. The rest of the docs are accurate and well organized.

architecture.overview:
`prefect sdk generate` is a beta Typer command in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`. It calls `generate_sdk` in `_sdk/generator.py`, which runs `fetch_sdk_data` in `_sdk/fetcher.py` against the Prefect API to build `SDKData` (flows, deployments, work pools). `render_sdk` in `_sdk/renderer.py` then fills the `templates/sdk.py.jinja` template into a typed Python module with `deployments.from_name()`, `with_options()`, `with_infra()`, and `run()`/`run_async()`.

This PR does not change the runtime pipeline. It adds documentation for it: a how-to guide (`generate-custom-sdk.mdx`), a CLI reference page (`api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx`), and navigation entries in `docs.json`. It also changes the fetcher's deployment-name filter and a few adjacent details, which affect which deployments end up in the generated SDK and which warnings are emitted.
steps: Entry point: the user runs `prefect sdk generate --output ... [--flow] [--deployment]`. Typer parses the options in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`, and the command help text is the source for `api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx`.

`generate_sdk` in `_sdk/generator.py` calls `fetch_sdk_data`. The fetcher builds a flow filter and a deployment filter, then sends them to a single `read_deployments` call, so the two filters are ANDed on the server.

Inside `fetch_sdk_data`, the deployment-name loop matches short names (`production`) and full names (`my-flow/production`). It records short-name matches so it can warn about ambiguity. This PR changes the gate condition for that loop (fetcher.py:397).

`render_sdk` turns the resulting `SDKData` into the typed module. Work pool `job_variables_schema` drives the `with_infra()` type hints, so the fetcher's work pool handling feeds the generated API surface.
The PR adds `generate-custom-sdk.mdx` as the user-facing guide. Its examples are checked against the template methods, and its combined-filter example is wrong given the AND semantics above.
Navigation: `docs.json` adds the guide under a new Deployments group in Advanced and the CLI reference under the CLI list. It also moves the unrelated form-building page into that group.

findings.title: Deployment-name gate change drops the ambiguous short-name warning
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` around line 397, the deployment filter gate was changed from `full_name not in deployment_names` to `dep.name not in deployment_names`. Revert it to compare `full_name`. The short-name branch and the ambiguity bookkeeping depend on that condition being entered for short-name filters, and `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py::test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` covers this. If the intent was a different fix, describe it in the PR and add a test for the full-name and short-name cases.

findings.title: Combined-filter example in the guide fails because filters are ANDed
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx`, the "Combine multiple filters" example (around lines 40-46) passes two `--flow` values and a `--deployment analytics/daily`. Flow and deployment filters are ANDed in `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` (`_fetch_deployments` sends both to one `read_deployments` call), so the example returns no deployments. Rewrite the example to a combination that matches, for example a single `--flow` plus a `--deployment` whose flow is that same flow. Add one sentence stating that filters combine with AND. Do not change the fetcher.

findings.title: Removing the dict guard lets non-dict job variables reach the renderer
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` in `_fetch_work_pool` (around lines 180-182), the `isinstance(variables, dict)` guard was removed when assigning `job_vars_schema` from `base_job_template["variables"]`. Restore the guard, or otherwise make sure a non-dict value is normalized to `{}` before it is stored in `WorkPoolInfo.job_variables_schema`. Check the consumer at `src/prefect/_sdk/renderer.py` around line 271 to confirm the expected type. Add a test for a non-dict `variables` value in `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py`.

findings.title: Module-level logger inserted between imports fails ruff E402
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, the module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (around lines 19-21) sits in the middle of the import block, which triggers ruff E402 on the following `from prefect...` imports. Move the logger definition to after the last import (after the `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block) so all imports stay at the top. Then run `ruff check src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` and confirm it is clean.

findings.title: Removed strict=True from zip without explanation
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` around line 220 in `_fetch_work_pools_parallel`, `strict=True` was removed from `zip(pool_names_list, results)`. Restore `strict=True`. Both sequences are the same length by construction, so the guard should never fire.

findings.title: Reorganizing docs navigation moves an unrelated page
findings.body:
`docs/docs.json` moves `v3/advanced/form-building` out of the Advanced list into a new "Deployments" group. The new group holds the SDK guide and the form-building page. Form-building is about flow parameter forms, not deployments, so the new grouping is misleading, and the move is not mentioned in the PR description. Keep form-building where it was and add only the new SDK guide. If a new group is needed, give it a name that fits both pages.

::diff{file="docs/docs.json" lines="263-268"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/docs.json`, the Advanced navigation was changed to move `v3/advanced/form-building` into a new "Deployments" group together with `v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk` (around lines 255-268). Put `v3/advanced/form-building` back in its original position in the Advanced pages list. Keep only `v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk` in the navigation for this PR, placed where it fits, or in a group whose name accurately describes both pages.

findings.title: CLI reference omits short flags and the required --output marker
findings.body:
The Typer command in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py` declares `-o`, `-f`, and `-d` short aliases, and `--output` is a required option (`typer.Option(...)`). `api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx` lists the long names only and doesn't say that `--output` is required. Users reading the reference will be surprised when the command fails without `--output`. The PR says this page is auto-generated, so if the generator omits this metadata, the cause is upstream and should be fixed there. Otherwise, add the aliases and the required marker by hand.

::code{file="docs/v3/api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx" lines="66-72"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/v3/api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx`, the Options accordion (around lines 66-72) lists `--output`, `--flow`, and `--deployment` without their short aliases (`-o`, `-f`, `-d`) from `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`, and does not say `--output` is required. If this page is generated, fix the generator. Otherwise add the aliases and a required marker by hand, matching the format used by other CLI reference pages in `docs/v3/api-ref/cli/`.

findings.title: Guide API usage matches the generated template
findings.body: The guide's method names and options match what `templates/sdk.py.jinja` generates: `deployments.from_name()`, `.with_options()` with `tags`, `idempotency_key`, `work_queue_name`, `as_subflow`, `scheduled_time`, and `flow_run_name`, `.with_infra()`, `.run()` and `.run_async()`, which return a `PrefectFlowRunFuture` exposing `flow_run_id`. The CLI reference text also matches the Typer help strings in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`. Reviewers can spot-check the docs against the template without guessing.
